studies.title: River confluence
studies.purpose: Three banks form separate campaign areas. Two crossings approach Bellweather; a downstream crossing links the outer banks without using the centre.
studies.departures: Bellweather can directly connect to mixed and outlying districts. Regions occupy separate banks, and bridges restore specific district connections.
studies.watch: The downstream crossing could matter more than either central crossing if players can satisfy regional objectives without approaching Bellweather.

studies.title: Lake city
studies.purpose: A continuous shoreline offers clockwise and anticlockwise approaches to the same targets, while the lake removes direct shortcuts across the middle.
studies.departures: Bellweather sits on a shore rather than at the geographic centre. Regional boundaries follow stretches of shoreline rather than concentric bands.
studies.watch: The two directions may feel equivalent unless starting Support creates different costs along them.

studies.title: Mountain pass
studies.purpose: Two inhabited passes connect the valleys; a longer southern foothill route provides a third approach around the mountains.
studies.departures: Dense districts are split across the valleys and passes. Regions need not be geographically contiguous, and Bellweather itself occupies a pass.
studies.watch: Passing through Bellweather may become incidental to valley-to-valley travel rather than an elective investment in Capital scoring.

studies.title: River delta
studies.purpose: Four inhabited delta islands form a circuit. A party can approach an island from either neighboring island, but cannot jump between diagonal islands.
studies.departures: Districts form island groups independent of scoring regions. Bridges, rather than shared land borders, connect the groups.
studies.watch: If each island can be developed in isolation, the circuit may be safe expansion rather than a reason to interfere.

studies.title: Walled city
studies.purpose: Four gates connect a compact old city to an outer circuit. Different gates give access to different inner districts.
studies.departures: The urban region and Bellweather lie inside a wall. Gate connections replace ordinary proximity across that wall.
studies.watch: Four gates may make the wall easy to bypass; compare which gates actually attract Support rather than assuming all are valuable.

studies.title: Twin cities
studies.purpose: Two substantial banks support separate concentrations of activity. Three crossings connect different pairs of neighborhoods.
studies.departures: Dense cities occupy both banks: the three urban-region cities remain together on the west bank, while mixed-region Northgate lies on the east. Other scoring regions extend across both banks.
studies.watch: Cross-bank scoring could make a coalition or remote-placement bonus more efficient than repeatedly using bridges.

studies.title: Peninsula capital
studies.purpose: The urban port occupies a peninsula behind two approaches from the mainland. Bellweather sits near its tip, while the broader scoring landscape remains inland.
studies.departures: The city follows an elongated peninsula rather than a fan. Open water surrounds the peninsula, and access to its tip follows land routes.
studies.watch: If Capital scoring remains small compared with regional scoring, travelling down the peninsula may rarely be worth the actions.

studies.title: Island chain
studies.purpose: One urban island faces a central Bellweather island, with a looping chain of mixed and outlying territories around them.
studies.departures: Districts fill their islands: shared borders define adjacency for every effect, and only marked bridges connect across water. All three urban districts share one island. Bellweather occupies its own central island and connects to all three regions. The sheet is landscape A4 with a six-year tracker below the map.
studies.watch: Compare the direct bridges through Bellweather with the outer island loop. Watch whether a full urban island makes access to the mixed region too dependent on Grand Market, and whether the outer rural bridges remain attractive.

studies.title: Crescent bay
studies.purpose: An inner coastal route and an outer inland route follow the same broad bay. Connections between them allow players to change approach without crossing water.
studies.departures: The shoreline remains open and unbridged. Districts occupy two curved bands, with Bellweather one stop on the coastal band.
studies.watch: The outer band may become a faster bypass if its connections let players skip too many coastal districts.

studies.title: Railway junction
studies.purpose: Intersecting rail corridors divide the city into four sectors. Road viaducts connect the sectors in a circuit away from the rail junction.
studies.departures: Rail infrastructure blocks adjacency just like water. Bellweather is near the junction but has no special connection through the tracks.
studies.watch: The four sectors may function like separate boards unless players have objectives on both sides of a viaduct.

studies.title: Ridge city
studies.purpose: The urban districts form a ridge-top route above two lower neighborhoods. Several hillside approaches connect the slopes to different ridge districts.
studies.departures: The urban region is elongated along high ground. Scoring regions occupy different elevations and connect through explicit hillside routes.
studies.watch: The ridge could become a compulsory highway rather than one of several useful approaches; look for overused central ridge districts.

studies.title: Estuary city
studies.purpose: The river widens toward the coast, leaving both crossings upstream. A campaign on the lower opposite bank requires a substantial inland detour.
studies.departures: Opposite coastal districts have no crossing despite being visually close. Dense cities occupy both banks, but the three urban-region cities remain on the west; other scoring regions span the river.
studies.watch: Low coastal districts may become quiet scoring pockets because reinforcement from the opposite bank takes too long.

studies.title: Crater city
studies.purpose: Bellweather sits on the crater floor. Four breaks in the rim connect the inner neighborhoods to an outer circuit.
studies.departures: The mixed region shares the crater floor with the urban districts. The rim separates travel areas rather than perfectly matching scoring regions.
studies.watch: The central floor may offer such short routes that the outer circuit becomes a collection of destinations rather than a useful route.

studies.title: Industrial belt
studies.purpose: Large industrial sites leave two service corridors between east and west. Districts on either side of a factory are not automatically adjacent.
studies.departures: Non-playable industrial footprints divide the city. Access follows the two service corridors, and scoring regions can span the belt.
studies.watch: Two crossings may make the center feel obstructive rather than contested if most points can be earned on either bank independently.

studies.title: Greenbelt city
studies.purpose: An urban core is separated from satellite settlements by a greenbelt. Four access corridors connect different parts of the core to the outer circuit.
studies.departures: Protected land is a true adjacency barrier for this study. Outer scoring regions need not each have their own direct connection to Bellweather.
studies.watch: If the access corridors are too interchangeable, the greenbelt may add travel without producing meaningful decisions.

studies.title: Floodplain city
studies.purpose: Raised settlements connect through an embankment network above wet lowlands. The geography emphasizes which raised roads offer alternate approaches.
studies.departures: Only the printed embankments are usable connections; open-looking low ground is not automatically traversable. All roads are treated as permanent in this study.
studies.watch: A few highly connected settlements could dominate the raised network. Seasonal flooding is deliberately not assumed.

studies.title: Market crossroads
studies.purpose: Four market approaches meet at Bellweather, with outer settlement routes that can bypass the central crossroads.
studies.departures: Bellweather directly connects to a mixed city as well as urban districts. The centre is a transport junction, not a protected urban-only destination.
studies.watch: Direct traffic through Bellweather may make Capital scoring too easy or turn the centre into the strongest Smear position.
